transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Thank you for fitting me in, doctor. I, um... I hope I’m not wasting your time. I really don't want to come across as a difficult person or a complainer—I'm usually very easy to get along with. Is it alright if I just explain a bit about what's been going on at my home? 

It’s just... well, for months now, the property manager and certain people in my building have been doing these things. I wouldn't even bring it up if it wasn't so persistent, but they've been using, you know, deliberately misdelivered mail, and these perfectly timed noises in the walls, plus little comments from the neighbors... all to pressure me out of the apartment. 

I know how it might sound, and I hope you don't think I'm overreacting, but as a management analyst, my whole career is based on recognizing trends. They keep offering me paperwork and innocent-sounding explanations, but no amount of their excuses changes the pattern I can clearly see. Does... does that make sense why I'd be stressed about that?
Do you believe for certain that your property manager and neighbors are deliberately trying to force you out of the apartment?

Well... yes. I really wish I didn't have to say that, because I know it probably makes me sound difficult or stubborn, and I promise you I'm really not. I'd much rather just be on good terms with everyone. But... yes, I am absolutely certain. 

Like I was saying, with the misdelivered mail, and those noises in the walls that happen at the exact same times, plus the little comments from the neighbors... it's all very clearly coordinated to pressure me out of the apartment. They do try to smooth it over, of course. They'll hand me maintenance paperwork or give these very innocent-sounding explanations, but... none of that changes the pattern I can see with my own eyes. 

I hope you can understand why I can't just ignore that? I'm not trying to be unreasonable, I'm just looking at the facts, you know?
Have you heard voices when no one else is there?

Oh, no. No, nothing like that. I... I hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm, well, losing my grip on reality or anything. I don't hear voices in my head. I know that would be a completely different sort of problem, and I promise you I'm very grounded. 

When I hear people talking, it's just the actual neighbors out in the hall or, you know, making their little comments where they know I can hear them. Just real people. I really want to make sure I'm answering you correctly, though—is that what you were asking about?
Have you generally found it hard to trust other people for most of your adult life?

Oh, gosh, no. No, not at all. I... I really hope I haven't come across as cynical or, you know, suspicious by nature. I've actually always prided myself on being a very trusting person. 

In my career, working with different teams and clients, you really have to build good, solid relationships, and I've always gotten along wonderfully with my colleagues. I usually try to see the best in everyone. That's... well, that's honestly why this whole situation at the building has been so upsetting for me, because it's just not how I normally interact with the world. I'd much rather just trust people and go with the flow. 

Does... does that make sense? I just really want to make sure you know I'm usually a very agreeable guy, and I don't make a habit of doubting people's intentions.
Have you been experiencing this situation with your neighbors and property manager for longer than one month?

Well... yes, it has. I, um... I feel a little embarrassed admitting how long it's actually been going on, because I know I probably should have brought it up to someone sooner. But I really didn't want to make a fuss or be a nuisance to anyone. 

It's been... gosh, about 11 months now. It started shortly after I moved into the new apartment. I just kept hoping things would settle down and we could all just get along, you know? I'd always rather give people the benefit of the doubt. I hope it's okay that I tried to just endure it and handle it myself for so long... I'm answering your questions alright, aren't I?
Since this started, has your ability to work or manage your day-to-day life become much worse?

Well... I wouldn't say it's become much worse. I mean, I'm still very capable, I promise you that. I really don't want you to think I'm just letting my life fall apart, because I've always been very organized and on top of things. 

But... I suppose I have had to, um, pull back from several of my consulting jobs lately. I feel a little embarrassed admitting it, but I've just been spending so much of my week following up with the neighbors, and calling the offices, and checking in with the building staff. Just trying to sort it all out properly, you know? Make sure everyone is on the same page. 

It just ends up taking so much time that I haven't really been able to settle into my normal work, or even my painting routine, which I usually find so relaxing. I really hope that doesn't make me sound irresponsible or lazy. I just felt like I had to address the situation at the building before I could focus on everything else. Am I explaining that alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Has anything happened that made you think your neighbors or the property manager can control your thoughts or put thoughts into your mind?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. I... I really wouldn't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or anything. I know my own mind, I promise you. 

I mean, they're certainly making my life difficult, and they're coordinating against me, but they can't... they can't get inside my head or control what I think. I'm still very sharp, you know? I've always had a very clear mind, and I still do. I just... I just want them to stop interfering with my life and my apartment. 

That... that sounds reasonable, doesn't it? I just want to make sure I'm not coming across as, well, unreasonable or... or crazy. I'm just a normal guy dealing with a very frustrating situation. I hope I'm making sense.
Have you noticed yourself becoming emotionally flat or unable to feel much interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I still very much enjoy the things I've always enjoyed. I... I really don't want you to think I'm depressed or just giving up on life. I've always been a very positive, upbeat person.

I suppose I haven't been painting quite as much lately, like I mentioned, but that's really just because I've been so preoccupied with trying to sort out this whole situation at the building. It's not that I don't *want* to paint, or that I don't find it pleasurable anymore. It's just... well, it's hard to relax and focus on a canvas when you're constantly worried about what the neighbors are planning next, you know? 

But my feelings are still very much intact, I assure you. I still love a good cup of coffee in the morning, and I still enjoy reading my history books when I can find a quiet moment. I'm still very much myself. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I'm doing.
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t make sense to them?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I pride myself on being a very clear communicator. In my line of work as a management analyst, you really have to be, you know? I've always been very structured in how I speak and present my thoughts. 

I... I really hope I haven't been rambling or jumping around too much today? I'm trying very hard to be concise and give you exactly what you need. Sometimes I know I can get a little caught up in explaining the details of what's happening at the building, just because it's so complex, but people usually tell me I'm very easy to understand. 

I certainly wouldn't want you to think my mind is disorganized or that I can't hold a proper conversation. I'm doing okay explaining things to you today, aren't I? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
At any point during this past year, have you heard voices speaking to you or about you when no one was actually there?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I've never experienced anything like that. I... I know that's something that happens to some people, but it's certainly never happened to me. 

My hearing is perfectly fine, and I only hear people when they're actually speaking. Sometimes I might overhear the neighbors whispering through the walls, but that's just them actually talking, not... not anything imaginary. I'm very grounded in reality, I promise. 

I hope you don't think I'm the sort of person who hears things that aren't there? I'm just a normal, rational man trying to explain a very real situation. My answers are still making sense, aren't they? I'm really trying my best to give you the information you need.

During this past year, was there ever a period of at least one month when the neighbors’ comments or messages felt so direct and unmistakable that you believed they were clearly talking about you in public or sending you special messages through ordinary events?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I mean, I don't think they're... sending me secret codes through the television or, or arranging things on the street to send me a message. I'm not... I know some people struggle with those kinds of thoughts, but I'm very rational about all of this. 

When I talk about the neighbors, it's just the things I actually hear them saying through the walls, or the way they look at me in the hallway. It's very ordinary, really, just... unpleasant. I certainly don't think the whole world is in on it or that ordinary events are about me. 

I hope that makes sense? I really want to be clear that I'm just dealing with a difficult situation in my building, not... not imagining things in the world around me. I'm being helpful, aren't I? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
